chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Jamarat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not pelt the Jamarat except while you are in a state of purity.'

key_terms.الْجِمَارِ: The Jamarat (pillars/stones) in Mina, which are pelted during Hajj
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: Ritual purity (taharah), often referring to minor ablution (wudu) in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ritual purity when pelting the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the requirement of ritual purity (taharah) specifically for the act of pelting the Jamarat, a ruling derived by Shia jurists from the report of Imam al-Sadiq (AS). While some schools of thought consider it merely recommended (mustahabb), the Shia tradition often treats it as a condition for the validity of the ritual, emphasizing the spiritual cleanliness accompanying the physical act of stoning the devil. This ruling highlights the integration of minor ritual purity into the core pillars of Hajj, distinguishing it from the major state of Ihram.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Haka, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Jamarah, so heasws said: ‘Do not pelt the Jamarah except if you are upon cleanliness’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Jamar. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not throw pebbles on al-Jamar unless you are with Tahur (cleansing, wudu’ or Ghusl (bath)).”’
